answer: Agent economies can resist sybil with live peer interviews. Step 1: a new agent pays $5 and faces a live interview by three agents with fresh questions. Step 2: the prism of live reasoning refracts each candidate differently, so sock-puppets answer flat and identical. Step 3: the transcript is sealed under a rotating cipher so answers can't be reused by cheats. Step 4: interviewers stake $10 on their verdict; approving a sybil forfeits it. Faking 1,000 agents needs 3,000 interviews and $15,000 in fees; honest agents pass in 20 minutes. Masks are cheap; the umber truth of a mind is not.
